title: Make your first beat
description: Start small: a drum pattern, a bass part and a simple arrangement. Finish a short idea before collecting more tools.
outcome: A saved session and a short beat export you can listen to away from your workstation.

steps.label: Set up one workstation
steps.action: Choose one DAW that runs on your device. Create a project, choose a comfortable tempo and save it in a dedicated folder.

steps.label: Build a four-bar groove
steps.action: Use an included drum instrument to place a kick, snare and hi-hat pattern. Loop four bars and change one rhythm or velocity at a time.

steps.label: Add bass and a musical idea
steps.action: Choose a few notes from one scale. Make a bass part and a short melody, leaving space so the drums still feel clear.

steps.label: Arrange and export a first draft
steps.action: Duplicate the loop into a short arrangement. Remove or add parts for contrast, lower any clipping channels, export and listen to the file from beginning to end.

steps.label: Keep track of your sounds
steps.action: List the sources of any downloaded sounds. Save their terms and required credits before sharing your beat publicly.

title: Produce music

steps.label: Pick a DAW
steps.action: Choose one workstation that fits your device. Create a project folder and save an empty session before adding sounds.

steps.label: Check edu pricing
steps.action: If you qualify, compare the vendor's current education terms with its standard license. Check renewal and upgrade conditions before buying.

steps.label: Free instruments
steps.action: Choose one instrument and make a four-bar part. Use the included sounds first, and note the license for any downloaded presets or samples.

steps.label: Learn mixing basics
steps.action: Arrange your parts, set levels before effects, then compare quietly with a reference you know. Make one change at a time and save a new version.

steps.label: License checklist
steps.action: Review every external asset and keep its source, permission and credit requirements alongside the session.

description: Learn music production and mixing through a small, repeatable session: one DAW, a few instruments and deliberate listening.
outcome: A short arrangement with balanced levels and a saved project you can reopen.

title: Rapper & independent artist
description: Create a repeatable writing, recording and release workflow with clear permissions and organized sessions.
outcome: A vocal demo with an organized session, contributor notes and a next revision plan.

steps.label: Choose a beat and check permissions
steps.action: Use an original beat or read the specific license for a licensed beat. Confirm the permitted release and keep the agreement with the project.

steps.label: Write and rehearse a short section
steps.action: Write a verse or hook, rehearse it against the beat and record a rough voice memo. Mark breath points and revise lines that feel rushed.

steps.label: Record clean, organized takes
steps.action: Record a level test and listen for clipping, room noise and headphone bleed. Name each take and keep the original recordings before choosing a comp.

steps.label: Balance the voice and beat
steps.action: Start with level and panning. Check that the words remain clear at quiet volume, and compare edits before adding more effects.

steps.label: Prepare credits and a release plan
steps.action: Record contributors and agreed credits, gather permissions and choose a realistic next action: revise the demo, share privately for feedback or prepare a release.

title: Build a responsible sample workflow
description: Make source and permission records part of the creative process, from download to final credits.
outcome: A sample folder with traceable sources, saved terms and credits for your intended project.

steps.label: Choose a traceable source
steps.action: Find a sound on the original library or creator page. Record its file or pack name, creator and source URL; avoid download mirrors with unclear ownership.

steps.label: Read the exact asset terms
steps.action: Check the license for the particular file and your intended use. Look for attribution, commercial-use, redistribution and modification conditions. If unclear, use another asset or ask the owner.

steps.label: Save permission records with the audio
steps.action: Keep a copy of the terms, download date, purchase receipt when relevant and required credit text alongside the original audio.

steps.label: Build and document your session
steps.action: Import working copies, label sample tracks clearly and record which assets appear in the finished arrangement. Keep originals separate from edited versions.

steps.label: Review credits before publishing
steps.action: Match the final project against your asset list, add required credits and check whether the intended release fits the saved terms. Recheck any changed terms or unresolved permission questions.

title: Game & interactive audio

steps.label: Legal SFX libraries
steps.action: Choose a small set of sound effects from the original source. Save each file's terms and credit text with the asset.

steps.label: Middleware (FMOD / Wwise)
steps.action: Decide whether your project needs middleware. Follow the official introductory material and make a single event respond to a parameter.

steps.label: Engine audio docs
steps.action: Connect one sound to an in-game action. Test its volume, looping and behavior when the action repeats or stops.

steps.label: Ship a jam build
steps.action: Build a small scene, test audio in the exported game and include required credits. Ask a collaborator to try it on another device.

description: Move from a sound folder to a small interactive scene, with a repeatable test and credits workflow.
outcome: A playable scene with a triggered sound, a tested mix and asset credits.

title: Podcast & video

steps.label: Record & edit
steps.action: Record a short voice test, listen on headphones, then edit a two-minute segment. Keep an untouched copy of the original recording.

steps.label: Stream routing
steps.action: Route your microphone and playback to the recorder deliberately. Make a private test recording to catch missing sources, feedback or doubled audio.

steps.label: Host & publish
steps.action: Compare hosting terms and export requirements at the source. Prepare a title, description and credits, then listen to the full exported file.

steps.label: Captions & a11y
steps.action: Create captions or a transcript, check names and technical words, and confirm the text matches the published audio.

description: Build a recording and publishing routine for spoken audio, video or a live stream.
outcome: A short edited recording with checked routing and an accessible transcript.

title: Film & YouTube mix

steps.label: Edit dialog
steps.action: Organize dialogue takes, trim distracting gaps and use short fades at edits. Listen for consistency before adding processing.

steps.label: LUFS / loudness
steps.action: Check your destination's current loudness and true-peak specification. Measure the finished export with a suitable meter; a reference value alone is not a measurement.

steps.label: Clear samples
steps.action: Check the exact license for each music cue and sound effect, including your intended distribution and any attribution requirements.

steps.label: License checklist
steps.action: Collect permissions and credits, review the final video from start to finish, and archive the delivered version with its project files.

description: Make speech easy to follow and prepare a video mix with organized sources and delivery checks.
outcome: An intelligible dialogue edit and an export checked against your destination's requirements.

title: Release a track

steps.label: Master / loudness (learn)
steps.action: Compare your final mix at matched listening level and check the export for clipping or missing endings. Read the destination's format requirements before delivery.

steps.label: Sample licenses filed
steps.action: Keep source URLs, receipts, permission records and required credits for every external sample or beat. Resolve unclear permissions before publishing.

steps.label: Distribution
steps.action: Compare current distributor terms, prepare artist and contributor metadata, confirm artwork permissions and check the uploaded audio before submitting.

description: Turn a finished session into a release package with deliberate audio, rights and delivery checks.
outcome: A checked audio export, an asset-permissions folder and a release metadata sheet.
